newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end near new all-time highs.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end near new all-time highs.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply higher and near new all-time highs set late in the day as broad-based buying returned to the cash market.
"It was a strong cash close," said one S&P 500 trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "They ignored the bond market all day," he said.

Index futures surged from the opening bell, despite weakness in the bond market throughout the day, which traders linked to Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips's remark that consumers will resume spending and make for a good holiday season for retailers.
Premiums widened during the advance, with arbitrage buy programs set off when the premium of December S&Ps over the spot index widened above 3.20 points, traders said.
Strength in over-the-counter stocks, and the technology sector in particular, fueled buying on the floor in index futures, the traders said.
Nikkei 225 index futures closely tracked the rise in U.S. stock indexes but trimmed their gains late in the session in light activity, they noted.
Some traders expected strength to continue, although activity next week could be light because of the U.S. holiday.

At settlement, December S&P 500s were up 5.75 points at 751.20, Russell 2000s rose 3.25 point to 351.25, Value Line futures were up 4.90 point to 678.20, Nikkei 225 index futures gained 85.0 to 21,260.0 and Midcap 400s advanced 2.10 points to 255.80. --Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750/email:derivatives@reuters.com
